chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Al-Sabbah Al-Kinany, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And those who do not witness Al-Zur,' he said: 'It is Al-Gina' (singing/music).'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic term 'Al-Zur' refer to according to Imam al-Sadiq (as)?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) offers a specific exegetical interpretation of Surah Al-Furqan 25:72, equating 'Al-Zur' (falsehood or egregious sin) with 'Al-Gina' (singing/music). This identification serves as a primary textual basis in Shia jurisprudence for the prohibition of listening to and performing music, framing it not merely as a cultural preference but as a distinct category of sin linked to divine revelation. The brevity of the report highlights the Imam's authority to clarify ambiguous Quranic terms, establishing a direct theological link between musical entertainment and spiritual impurity.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, and Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinany,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [25:72] And they who are not witnessing (attending) what is false. Heasws said: ‘It is the singing (music)’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim and abu ai-Sabbah af-Kinaniy who has said the following:
“About the meaning of the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘. . . those who do not attend al-Zur . . .’ [25:72] abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘It is music (and singing).”’
